items.reason: R2 correctly restored "canvas" (the canvas cloth). The paragraph still flattens two points of Melville's mock-grandeur: the harpooneers as the feast's "residuary legatees" (a legal joke) becomes "leftover heirs of the feast", and "the high and mighty cabin" (ironic) becomes "the grand cabin". Restore both with minimal wording.
items.new: Now, Ahab and his three mates formed what might be called the first table in the Pequod's cabin. After their departure, in reverse order of their arrival, the canvas tablecloth was cleared — or rather restored to some hasty order by the pale steward. Then the three harpooners were invited to the feast, being its residuary legatees — the heirs to whatever was left. They made a sort of temporary servants' hall of the high and mighty cabin.
